new.title: Four independently varying cyclic column modes on the four-by-five permanent level must each be a line (exploration)
new.statement:
∀ (ζ : ℂ), IsPrimitiveRoot ζ 5 →
  ∀ U : Fin 4 → Submodule ℂ (Fin 4 → ℂ),
    (∀ r, U r ≠ ⊥) →
    (∀ r, ∀ v ∈ U r, (∑ i, v i) = 0) →
    (∀ x : Fin 4 → Fin 4 → ℂ, (∀ r, x r ∈ U r) →
      (∑ f : Fin 4 ↪ Fin 5, ∏ i : Fin 4,
        (1 + ∑ r : Fin 4, x r i * ζ ^ ((r.val+1)*(f i).val))) = 120) →
    ∀ r, Module.finrank ℂ (U r) = 1
new.unlocks: Excludes a five-dimensional space made from all four independent column modes. Seat-gct-2 reads the return.
new.context: Relabel a doubled mode as mode 1. Write its centred columns in Hadamard coordinates, with plane U=(a,b,sa+tb). Pick nonzero y,z,w in modes 2,3,4. Extract the pair coefficients u·w=y·z=0, cubic z·q(u)=0 and quartics y·D(u)=w·D(y)=0, where qᵢ=uⱼuₖ and Dᵢ=uᵢ(2uᵢ²−Σuⱼ²). Normalize w=(-s,-t,1). If st is nonzero the cubic forces z=0. Otherwise swap axes so s=0. Coefficient comparison gives tz₁=tz₂+z₃=y₁=y₂+ty₃=0. For t nonzero the dot product gives ty₃z₂=0. At t=0 the last quartic gives y₃³=0. Both cases contradict the choices.

new.unlocks: Exploration of the smallest graphs on which one NOT gate can shorten a circuit for edge detection.
new.sketch: Exploration of one NOT on an eight-vertex graph. Test an AND/OR witness against all 256 inputs, then prove that shorter circuits with at most one NOT fail using a gate lower bound or an exhaustive certificate. For a saving, exhibit the one-NOT circuit and exclude every shorter or equal-sized AND/OR circuit. The graph reader will inspect the shared wires and the input of the NOT in each saving. An equality removes this graph from the search for a saving.

changed.title: Find a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit under the ranked cyclic witness negation bound
changed.statement:
∃ (n w : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (q : Fin (2 ^ n)),
  let I := n * 2 ^ (w + 1)
  ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (outBit : Fin n → Fin (I + C.size)),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack I C ∧
    (∀ table : Fin n → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
      let inputs := (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => List.ofFn (fun pat : Fin (2 ^ (w + 1)) =>
        table i (fun j => pat.val.testBit j.val)))).flatten
      let sols := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin (2 ^ n))).filter (fun z => ∀ i : Fin n,
        table i (fun j => z.val.testBit (n - 1 - ((i.val + j.val) % n))) = true)
      q.val < sols.card → ∃ z ∈ sols,
        (sols.filter (fun y => y.val < z.val)).card = q.val ∧
        ∀ pos : Fin n, (C.wires inputs).getD (outBit pos).val false =
          z.val.testBit (n - 1 - pos.val)) ∧
    ∃ k b : ℕ, 0 < k ∧ k ≤ w + 1 ∧ k + b ≤ n ∧ q.val < 2 ^ (k + b) ∧
      2 ^ PEqualNP.NotBracket.notCount C <
        1 + ((n - b) / k) * (2 ^ k - 1) - q.val / 2 ^ b

changed.title: A reversible binary shift register realizes any XOR translation at every length at least its width
changed.statement:
∀ (d L : Nat),
  let w := d+1
  let State := Fin w → Bool
  ∀ target : State,
    (∃ (taps : Fin L → Fin d → Bool) (bias : Fin L → Bool), ∀ x : State,
      (List.finRange L).foldl (fun (s : State) row =>
        let z : Fin d → Bool := fun j => s j.succ
        let feedback := (List.finRange d).foldl
          (fun acc bit => xor acc (taps row bit && z bit)) (xor (s 0) (bias row))
        Fin.snoc (α := fun _ : Fin w => Bool) z feedback) x =
          (fun pos => xor (x pos) (target pos))) ↔
      w ≤ L ∨ (L = 0 ∧ ∀ coord, target coord = false)
changed.unlocks: pads a guarded register translation to every allowed cyclic block length
changed.context: For L=w take the full binary code. For L>=2w duplicate w consecutive generator columns of the length L-w code; windows inside the doubled basis are rotations. For w<L<2w take the orthogonal complement of the dimension L-w code; a dual word zero on w consecutive positions vanishes on each complementary unit vector. Consecutive windows are bases, giving feedback with coefficient one on the departing bit. Offset the final w bits. Below w a shift keeps another coordinate. The object is a list of affine rows priced by length, with no gates, so a cheaper circuit companion cannot exist.

changed.title: Adaptive word queries for a hidden binary majority gap obey a seed-count tradeoff and pay a length cost for either one-sided error
changed.statement:
∀ (n s : ℕ), 3 ≤ s → s ≤ n →
  let W := Fin n → Bool
  let Lit := Fin n × Bool
  let F := Finset (Lit × Lit)
  let sat := fun (C : F) (w : W) => decide (∀ c ∈ C,
    w c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ w c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2)
  let count := fun (G : F) => (Finset.univ.filter (fun u => sat G u = true)).card
  let Q := 2 ^ n
  ∀ (M q fp fn : ℕ), fp + fn < M →
    ∀ (ask : Fin M → List Bool → W) (report : Fin M → List Bool → Bool),
      let yes := fun (A : F) => (Finset.univ.filter (fun seed : Fin M =>
        let history := (List.range q).foldl (fun (past : List Bool) _ =>
          past ++ [sat A (ask seed past)]) []
        report seed history = true)).card
      (∀ A : F, 2 * count A ≤ Q → yes A ≤ fp) →
      (∀ A : F, Q * (2 ^ (s - 1) + 1) ≤ 2 ^ s * count A → M ≤ yes A + fn) →
      2 ^ (s - 1) * (M - fp - fn) ≤ q * (M - fp) ∧
      (fn = 0 → 2 ^ (s - 3) * Nat.clog 2 (2 * (n - s + 2) + 2) ≤ q) ∧
      (fp = 0 → 2 * n + 2 ≤ 2 ^ q)
changed.unlocks: bounds seed counts and query lengths for adaptive hidden majority decisions with either one-sided error
changed.context: Trace each seed on a unary half cube. A star adds one rare pattern on the center and s-1 leaves. Among R rejecting seeds, at least R-fn must hit each pattern on the baseline path, whereas each path hits at most q patterns. Sum and use R>=M-fp. With fn=0 one rejecting path covers every leaf pattern on every s-1 leaves. Slice by s-3 leaves, then count distinct signed columns and constants. With fp=0 take an accepting path on the full cube. A constant column or two equal or complementary columns give a unary or binary half-cube predicate with identical labels.

changed.title: Exact rational state dimension of a corrected cyclic syndrome trace at regular parameters
changed.statement:
∀ (r : ℕ) (z : ℚ),
  let A := Fin r → ZMod 2
  let q : ℕ := 2^r
  let f := fun a : A => if a = 0 then z-1 else -1
  let T : A → Matrix (Option A) (Option A) ℚ := fun h before after =>
    before.elim (after.elim 1 (fun b => if b = h then 1 else 0))
      (fun a => after.elim (f a) (fun b => if b = a+h then 1 else 0))
  let cycle := fun w : List A =>
    Matrix.trace (w.map T).prod + f w.sum - (if w.sum = 0 then (q : ℚ) else 0)
  let fits := fun (k : ℕ) (test : List A → Prop) =>
    ∃ (u v : Fin k → ℚ) (M : A → Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℚ),
      ∀ w : List A, test w → (∑ i : Fin k, ∑ j : Fin k, u i * (w.map M).prod i j * v j) = cycle w
  0 < r → z ≠ 0 → z ≠ 2 → z ≠ (q : ℚ) →
    let least : ℕ := (q+1)^2 + (if z = 2*(q : ℚ) then q-1 else q)
    ∀ k : ℕ, (fits k (fun _ => True) ↔ least ≤ k) ∧
      (fits k (fun w => 0 < w.length) ↔ least ≤ k)
changed.unlocks: Prices conversion of an entire corrected cyclic transfer summand into a rational linear scan, including the cost on positive cycle lengths alone.
changed.context: Fourier expansion gives the transfer trace and one scalar correction per character. Invert T0 to recover translations. Fourier projectors isolate each nontrivial character. An excursion through any one of these isolates empty inside the trivial block, giving all matrix units. The word algebra surjects onto the product of the matrix block and surviving characters. Its trace pairing is nondegenerate, giving the Hankel rank. Varying the empty word adds an independent scalar block. Full sketch in barriers/statements/graph-isotropic-code/cyclic-rank.sketch.txt.

changed.title: Exact state dimensions at the singular parameters of the corrected cyclic syndrome trace
changed.statement:
∀ (r : ℕ) (z : ℚ),
  let A := Fin r → ZMod 2
  let q : ℕ := 2^r
  let f := fun a : A => if a = 0 then z-1 else -1
  let T : A → Matrix (Option A) (Option A) ℚ := fun h before after =>
    before.elim (after.elim 1 (fun b => if b = h then 1 else 0))
      (fun a => after.elim (f a) (fun b => if b = a+h then 1 else 0))
  let cycle := fun w : List A =>
    Matrix.trace (w.map T).prod + f w.sum - (if w.sum = 0 then (q : ℚ) else 0)
  let fits := fun (k : ℕ) (test : List A → Prop) =>
    ∃ (u v : Fin k → ℚ) (M : A → Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) ℚ),
      ∀ w : List A, test w → (∑ i : Fin k, ∑ j : Fin k, u i * (w.map M).prod i j * v j) = cycle w
  (r = 0 ∨ z = 0 ∨ z = 2 ∨ z = (q : ℚ)) →
    let least : ℕ := if r = 0 then (if z = 1 then 1 else if z = 2 then 2 else 3)

    ∀ k : ℕ, (fits k (fun _ => True) ↔ least ≤ k) ∧

changed.title: Retaining the boundary XOR on hits increases scan gains under a gain-parity-preserving permutation and lowers the slot price at explicit depths
changed.statement:
let move := fun (keep : Bool) (mode letter : Nat) =>
  let near := letter.testBit 0
  let far := letter.testBit 1
  let hit := letter.testBit 2
  let aligned := ((mode == 1) && near && far) || ((mode == 2) && far) ||
    ((mode == 3) && near)
  let diagonal := (!hit && (((mode == 1) && !near && !far) ||
    (mode == 2) || (mode == 3))) || (keep && (mode == 3))
  (if aligned then (if hit then 0 else 2) else if diagonal then 3 else 1,
    hit.toNat + (aligned && hit).toNat)
let gain := fun (keep : Bool) (n code : Nat) =>
  ((List.range n).foldl (fun (st : Nat × Nat) pos =>
    let nxt := move keep st.1 ((code >>> (3*pos)) % 8)
    (nxt.1, st.2 + nxt.2)) (0,0)).2
let price := fun (keep : Bool) (n d : Nat) =>
  ((List.range (8^n)).map (fun word => 2^(2*n - (gain keep n word - d)))).sum
∀ n : Nat,
  (∃ perm : Fin (8^n) ≃ Fin (8^n), ∀ w : Fin (8^n),
    gain false n w.val ≤ gain true n (perm w).val ∧
    gain false n w.val % 2 = gain true n (perm w).val % 2) ∧
  ∀ d : Nat, price true n d ≤ price false n d ∧
    (price true n d < price false n d ↔ 4 ≤ n ∧ d+2 < 3*n/2)
changed.unlocks: Determines when retaining a hit gives the scheduled circuit a strictly smaller slot budget.
changed.context: Only the D-to-E transition of weight 2z changes. Factor the transfer-series difference through walks from E to D. Compare sorted gains of each parity. A length-j walk from E to D has maximum gain floor(3(j-1)/2), and the reciprocal determinant has degree floor(3l/2) at length l. A cheaper circuit companion cannot exist for this comparison of two scans under a permutation of their words because no gate count occurs.

changed.title: Widely spaced output bits bound the linear key queries needed to reduce a two-round parity to degree three
changed.statement:
∀ (k d : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k), 0 < d → 4 * d + 4 < k →
  let W := Fin k → Bool
  let idx := fun (n : ℕ) => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let add := fun (x y : W) (i : Fin k) => xor (x i) (y i)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (idx (i.val + k - s % k))
  let mix := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    xor (xor (x i) (x (idx (i.val + d)))) (x (idx (i.val + k - d)))
  let step := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    xor (x i) (!(x (idx (i.val + 1))) && x (idx (i.val + 2)))
  let diff := fun (f : W → Bool) (v x : W) => xor (f x) (f (add x v))
  let g := Nat.gcd k d
  let lost := if (k / g) % 3 = 0 then 2 * g else 0
  ∀ (s t h : ℕ) (name c₁ c₂ mask : W),
    let observed := fun (key : W) =>
      let initial := mix (add (rot s key) name)
      let middle := add (step initial) (add (rot t key) c₁)
      let out := add (step (mix middle)) (add (rot h key) c₂)
      (List.ofFn (fun bit : Fin k => mask bit && out bit)).foldl xor false
    ∀ (c : ℕ) (query : W → Fin c → Bool),
      (∀ x y i, query (add x y) i = xor (query x i) (query y i)) →
      ∀ (base : W),
        (∀ (v : Fin 4 → W) (x : W), query x = query base →
          (∀ j i, query (v j) i = false) →
          (List.ofFn v).foldl diff observed x = false) →
        let stride := 4 * d + 5
        let weight := (Finset.univ.filter (fun pos : Fin k => mask pos = true)).card
        (∀ chosen : Finset (Fin k), (∀ i ∈ chosen, mask i = true) →
          (∀ i ∈ chosen, ∀ j ∈ chosen, i ≠ j →
            stride ≤ (j.val + k - i.val) % k) → chosen.card ≤ c + lost) ∧
        (k / stride) * weight ≤ k * (c + lost)
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of linear key queries needed for a branchwise cubic two-round parity
changed.context: Each quartic fits in a cyclic interval of span D=2d+2. At selected positions spaced by 2D+1, free only the four extreme-product bits per interval. No quartic meets two intervals. Each contributes its unique degree-four product. In initial mixed coordinates take an affine section of the initial map. Its image costs h equations by the period-three kernel recurrence. The raw queries cost at most c more. Apply the disjoint-products bound. Average rotations of a stride-L packing for the weight inequality. Allow 60 minutes. A gate-saving companion cannot exist for a bound on linear queries.

changed.title: Disjoint comparisons against one baseline bound unrestricted gate count on two one-hot banks
changed.statement:
∀ (n m hr hc : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  let bounded := fun (i j : ℕ) (T : Fin i → Fin j → Bool) (h : ℕ) =>
    ∀ (off : Fin j → Bool) (F : Finset (Fin i × Fin i)),
      ((∀ e ∈ F, e.1 ≠ e.2 ∧
        (Finset.univ.filter (fun col => T e.1 col ≠ T e.2 col ∧ T e.1 col ≠ off col)).card ≤ 3) ∧
      (∀ e ∈ F, ∀ f ∈ F, e ≠ f →
        e.1 ≠ f.1 ∧ e.1 ≠ f.2 ∧ e.2 ≠ f.1 ∧ e.2 ≠ f.2)) → F.card ≤ h
  2*hr+2 ≤ n → 2*hc+2 ≤ m →
  (∀ a b : Fin n, a ≠ b → 6 ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun j => G a j ≠ G b j)).card) →
  (∀ a b : Fin m, a ≠ b → 6 ≤ (Finset.univ.filter (fun i => G i a ≠ G i b)).card) →
  bounded n m G hr → bounded m n (fun j i => G i j) hc →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C →
    13 * (n+m) ≤ 12*C.size + 36 + 2*(hr+hc)
changed.unlocks: turns the maximum number of disjoint compatible profile pairs into an unrestricted physical gate lower bound
changed.context: Normalize, then mark endpoints of a maximal matching of affordable pairs on each bank. An unread name sees every other name, so a matching among the others has size below h. Mark its endpoints and the unread name. A private piece has at most three opposite names by the four/six leaf bounds. Its zero/one-entry monotone sections are ordered, and the off section lies below both, so any two private rows form an affordable pair. Keep at most one unmarked per bank. Apply weighted slots with p=c=2 and collect the unread count. Allow 180 to 360 minutes.

changed.title: Two nonlinear gates cannot compute equality on sixteen one-hot labels at nonlinear depth two
changed.statement:
¬ (let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depth := fun (w : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  (C.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun a => ds.getD a 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate w 0)).getD C.output 0
∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
  (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack 32 C ∧
  PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 16 => decide (u = v)) C ∧
  depth 32 C ≤ 2 ∧ C.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ 2)
changed.unlocks: tests the two-product normal form against the rank of sixteen-label equality
changed.context: Express each input-affine form as a row term plus a column term over the binary field. In gate order write p=ab and q=(c+ep)(d+fp) with e,f bits. Expand p squared=p and absorb the affine output, obtaining a sum of products of one, two and three separated forms. Their table ranks are at most 2, 4 and 8, adding to at most 14. The target identity has rank 16. Allow 60 to 120 minutes.

changed.title: Perfect matching on a 3 by 3 graph: no normal-form circuit of at most 11 gates opens with AND of wires 0 and 1, then AND of wires 0 and 2
changed.statement:
¬ (∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 11 ∧
    (∀ x : Fin 9 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = ((x 0 && x 4 && x 8) || (x 0 && x 5 && x 7) || (x 1 && x 3 && x 8) || (x 1 && x 5 && x 6) || (x 2 && x 3 && x 7) || (x 2 && x 4 && x 6))) ∧
    C.output + 1 = 9 + C.size ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      ((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ∧
          ∃ a, a < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a]) ∨
      (((C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨
          (C.gates.get j).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or) ∧
          ∃ a b, a < b ∧ b < 9 + j.val ∧ (C.gates.get j).inputs = [a, b])) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length,
      (∃ x y : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn y)).getD (9 + j.val) false) ∧
      ∀ k, k < 9 + j.val → ∃ x : Fin 9 → Bool,
        (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD (9 + j.val) false ≠ (C.wires (List.ofFn x)).getD k false) ∧
    (∀ j : Fin C.gates.length, j.val + 1 < C.gates.length →
      ∃ k : Fin C.gates.length, j.val < k.val ∧ 9 + j.val ∈ (C.gates.get k).inputs) ∧
    C.gates.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [0, 1]⟩ ∧
    C.gates.tail.head? = some ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, [0, 2]⟩)
changed.sketch: A proof is one explicit counterexample to the positive statement L-meta-27133; none is expected if that statement is true.

changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat) (A : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (u : Fin n),
  (∃ i j, A i j = false) →
  ∀ (t s : Nat),
    let expanded := fun (i : Fin (n + t)) (j : Fin m) =>
      if h : i.val < n then A ⟨i.val, h⟩ j else A u j
    let extra := if ∃ (j : Fin m) (i : Fin n), A u j = true ∧ A i j = false
      then t else 0

      ∃ b : Nat, PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A b ∧ b + extra ≤ s

changed.context: If u accepts j rejected by i, the empty row bank rejects j, so each twin reaches a gate. Delete a twin and fold the first gate that reads it. Iterate. OR gives the upper. Otherwise all columns accepted by u are full. With none, substitute false for u. With one, substitute its raw column for u. With several, contract them to one. Restoring them costs one each by the strict column case using the surviving zero, before and after copying u. Cancel the equal costs.

changed.title: At odd widths divisible by three a ternary formula propagates all compatible scheduled name bits with at most four inverse branches per round
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : ℕ), k % 6 = 3 →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let V := Fin 5 × Fin k
  let word := fun (v : V → Bool) (track : Fin 5) =>
    ∑ j : Fin k, (v (track,j)).toNat * 2^j.val
  let agrees := fun (v : V → Bool) =>
    word v 3 = first (word v 2) (word v 0) ∧
    word v 4 = second (word v 2) (word v 1)
  let rounds := 128*(r+1)*(Nat.clog 2 k+1)
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (F : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Sum V (Fin m)))),
    m + (∑ C ∈ F, C.card) ≤ 8192*(k+1)*4^r ∧
    (∀ C ∈ F, C.card ≤ 3) ∧
    (∀ v : V → Bool, agrees v ↔ ∃ aux : Fin m → Bool,
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim v aux) (↑F : Set _)) ∧
    ∀ ρ : V → Option Bool, (∀ j : V, 2 ≤ j.1.val → ∃ b : Bool, ρ j = some b) →
      let seed : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) :=
        {l | ∃ raw : V, l.1 = Sum.inl raw ∧ ρ raw = some l.2}
      let advance := fun S : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) =>
        S ∪ {l | ∃ C ∈ F, l ∈ C ∧ ∀ other ∈ C, other ≠ l →
          PEqualNP.Search.negLit other ∈ S}
      let known := (advance^[rounds]) seed
      let complete := fun v : V → Bool => agrees v ∧
        ∀ (raw : V) (sign : Bool), ρ raw = some sign → v raw = sign
      ((¬ ∃ v, complete v) ↔ ∃ C ∈ F, ∀ l ∈ C, PEqualNP.Search.negLit l ∈ known) ∧
      ((∃ v, complete v) → ∀ raw : V, ∀ sign : Bool,
        (∀ v, complete v → v raw = sign) ↔ (Sum.inl raw, sign) ∈ known)

changed.title: Exact worst-case query budgets in a fixed number of adaptive rounds for group-labelled edge violations
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (G : Type) [Group G] [DecidableEq G]
  (E : Fin n → Fin n → G → Prop),
  (∀ u v g, E u v g → E v u g⁻¹) →
  let walk := fun (m : ℕ) (v : ℕ → Fin n) (s : ℕ → G) =>
    ∀ i < m, E (v i) (v (i+1)) (s i)
  let gain := fun (m : ℕ) (s : ℕ → G) => ((List.range m).map s).prod
  let pinsOK := fun (S : Finset (Fin n)) (z : Fin n → G) (R : ℕ) =>
    ∀ m ≤ R, ∀ v s, walk m v s → v 0 ∈ S → v m ∈ S →
      z (v m) = z (v 0) * gain m s
  let closedOK := fun radius : ℕ =>
    ∀ m ≤ radius, ∀ v s, walk m v s → v 0 = v m → gain m s = 1
  let Strategy := List (Finset (Fin n × G)) → Finset (Fin n)
  let history := fun (ask : Strategy) (x : Fin n → G) (t : ℕ) =>
    (List.range t).foldl (fun hist _ => hist ++ [(ask hist).image (fun u => (u, x u))]) []
  let batch := fun (ask : Strategy) (x : Fin n → G) (i : ℕ) => ask (history ask x i)
  let win := fun (ask : Strategy) (x : Fin n → G) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (r : ℕ) =>
    let seen := S ∪ (Finset.range r).biUnion (batch ask x)
    ∃ u ∈ seen, ∃ v ∈ seen, ∃ g, E u v g ∧ x v ≠ x u * g
  let balanced := fun (r t : ℕ) => (t/r)^(r-(t % r)) * (t/r+1)^(t % r)
  ∀ (S : Finset (Fin n)) (z : Fin n → G) (r Q : ℕ), 0 < r →
  ((∃ ask : Strategy, ∀ x : Fin n → G, (∀ u ∈ S, x u = z u) →
      (Finset.range r).sum (fun round => (batch ask x round).card) ≤ Q ∧ win ask x S r) ↔ ¬ pinsOK S z (balanced r (Q+r)) ∨ ¬ closedOK (balanced r (Q+r-1)))

changed.context: For pinned endpoints maximize the product of q_i+1. For a walk returning to its start use q at the initial nonempty batch and q_i+1 thereafter. Balancing the factors gives M(r,Q+r) and M(r,Q+r−1). Either witness can pick the schedule attaining its bound. For the converse fix the initial batch of size q before its answers. The extension criterion leaves all old and queried pins consistent through the best remaining radius for r−1 rounds and Q−q queries. Exclude all short walks returning to their start. Induction handles transcript-dependent spending.

changed.title: Public randomness gives an exact error threshold and seed divisor for split CNFs comparing cyclic count-parity prefixes
changed.statement:
∀ (d paddingLeft paddingRight : ℕ),
  let w := d + 1
  let D := 2 ^ w
  let m := D * D
  let L := (12 * w * D * (D + 2) + 1) * w
  let h := L + paddingLeft
  let k := L + paddingRight
  let n := h + k
  let pos := fun idx : ℕ => (⟨idx % n, Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.add_pos_left (Nat.add_pos_left (Nat.mul_pos (Nat.zero_lt_succ _) (Nat.zero_lt_succ _)) _) _)⟩ : Fin n)
  let Raw := fun length : ℕ => Fin length × (Fin (w + 1) → Bool)
  let parity := fun (P : Raw h → Bool) (R : Raw k → Bool) =>
    let good := fun x : Fin n → Bool =>
      (∀ i : Fin h, P (i, fun j => x (pos (i.val + j.val))) = true) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin k, R (i, fun j => x (pos (h + i.val + j.val))) = true
    (Finset.univ.filter good).card.testBit 0
  let same := fun (P Q : Raw h → Bool) => ∀ R : Raw k → Bool, parity P R = parity Q R
  ∀ s : ℕ, s ≤ m →
    let N := 2 ^ m
    let K := 2 ^ (m - s)
    let divisor := 2 ^ Nat.gcd m s - 1
    let period := (N - 1) / divisor
    let hits := (K - 1) / divisor
    let V := fun size : ℕ => Sum (Raw h) (Sum (Fin s) (Fin size))
    let possible := fun (r errors : ℕ) (small : Bool) =>
      ∃ (a b : ℕ)
        (F : Fin r → Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (V a)))
        (G : Fin r → Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (V b))),
        (small = true → ∀ c : Fin r,
          (∀ C ∈ F c, C.card ≤ 3) ∧ (∀ C ∈ G c, C.card ≤ 3) ∧
          a + b + (∑ C ∈ F c, C.card) + (∑ C ∈ G c, C.card) ≤
            96 * (h + s + 1) * (m + 1)) ∧
        ∀ P Q : Raw h → Bool,
          let accepts := fun coin : Fin r =>
            ∃ (z : Fin s → Bool) (u : Fin a → Bool) (v : Fin b → Bool),
              PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim P (Sum.elim z u)) (↑(F coin) : Set _) ∧
              PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim Q (Sum.elim z v)) (↑(G coin) : Set _)
          (same P Q → ∀ coin, accepts coin) ∧
          (¬same P Q → (@Finset.filter _ accepts (Classical.decPred _) Finset.univ).card ≤ errors)
    ∀ r : ℕ, 0 < r →
      (∀ errors, possible r errors false → r * (K - 1) ≤ errors * (N - 1)) ∧
      possible r (r / period * hits + min (r % period) hits) true ∧
      ((∃ errors, possible r errors false ∧ errors * (N - 1) = r * (K - 1)) ↔ period ∣ r)

changed.title: Representative sections detect contradictions and count surviving clauses under arbitrary private Boolean substitution
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (w : Fin n → ℕ), (∀ i, 0 < w i) →
  ∀ g : (i : Fin n) → (Fin (w i) → Bool) → Bool, (∀ i b, ∃ x, g i x = b) →
  let B := PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)
  let Raw := (i : Fin n) × Fin (w i)
  let Axiom := PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause Raw
  let Tape := (i : Fin n) → Bool → Fin (w i) → Bool
  let sections := (Finset.univ : Finset Tape).filter (fun s => ∀ i b, g i (s i b) = b)
  let block := fun (C : B) (x : Raw → Bool) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset Raw).filter (fun j => j.1 ∈ C.image Prod.fst)).image (fun j => (j, !(x j)))
  let copies := fun (C : B) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Raw → Bool)).filter (fun x =>
      ∀ l ∈ C, g l.1 (fun j => x ⟨l.1,j⟩) ≠ l.2)).image (block C)
  ∀ F : Finset B, (∀ C ∈ F, ∀ i, ¬ ((i,true) ∈ C ∧ (i,false) ∈ C)) →
    let allAx := F.biUnion copies
    let project := fun (A : Finset Axiom) (s : Tape) => F.filter (fun C =>
      block C (fun z => s z.1 (decide ((z.1,false) ∈ C)) z.2) ∈ A)
    let bad := fun {V : Type} (K : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)) =>
      ¬ PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfiable (K : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V))
    ∀ A : Finset Axiom, A ⊆ allAx →
      (bad A ↔ ∀ s ∈ sections, bad (project A s)) ∧
      ∀ C ∈ F, (copies C).card * (sections.filter (fun s => C ∈ project A s)).card =
        sections.card * (A ∩ copies C).card

changed.title: Exact parity query depth for a reported XOR of disjoint singleton guards at arbitrary targets
changed.statement:
∀ (blocks width spare depth : Nat), 2 ≤ blocks → 3 ≤ width →
  let F := ZMod 2
  let B := Fin width → F
  let V := (Fin blocks → B) × (Fin spare → F)
  let P := F × V
  let n := blocks*width + spare
  ∀ (center : Fin blocks → B) (tilt : V →ₗ[F] F) (offset : F),
    let label := fun x : V => tilt x + offset +
      ∑ i : Fin blocks, (if x.1 i = center i then (1 : F) else 0)
    let saved := if ∃ i : Fin blocks, center i = 0
      then width-1 else min blocks (width-1)
    let correct := fun (out : P → Bool) =>
      (∀ b : F, out (b,0) = false) ∧ (∀ x : V, x ≠ 0 → out (label x,x) = true)
    let adaptive := ∃ (ask : (j : Fin depth) → (Fin j.val → F) → (P →ₗ[F] F))
        (ans : P → Fin depth → F) (read : (Fin depth → F) → Bool),
      (∀ (p : P) (j : Fin depth), ans p j =
        ask j (fun prev => ans p ⟨prev.val, Nat.lt_trans prev.isLt j.isLt⟩) p) ∧
      correct (fun p => read (ans p))
    let fixed := ∃ (Q : P →ₗ[F] (Fin depth → F)) (read : (Fin depth → F) → Bool),
      correct (fun p => read (Q p))
    And (Iff adaptive (n-saved ≤ depth)) (Iff fixed (n ≤ depth))

Otherwise use one guard per possible first 1 in a punctured hyperplane and choose a disjoint partner in the guard-free space. changed.title: Four boundary bits determine the exact parity-query cost for products in overlapping five-bit windows
changed.statement:
∀ (h t : ℕ) (a b : Fin h → Fin t → Fin 32) (d : ℕ),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin (h+4) → F
  let D := W →ₗ[F] F
  let operand := fun (x : W) (i : Fin h) (mask : Fin 32) =>
    ∑ j : Fin 5, if mask.val.testBit j.val then x (Fin.ofNat (h+4) (i.val+j.val)) else 0
  let run := fun (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (x : W) =>
    (List.finRange d).foldl (fun tr j => 2*tr + (if ask j tr x = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
  let advance := fun (st : ℕ × Finset ℕ) (atSite : Fin t → ℕ) =>
    let extended := (List.finRange t).foldl (fun (s : Finset ℕ) j =>
      s ∪ s.image (fun v => v ^^^ atSite j)) st.2
    let even := extended.filter (fun v => v % 2 = 0)
    (st.1 + (if even = extended then 0 else 1), even.image (fun v => v / 2))
  let selectMask := fun (u v : Fin 32) (c : Fin 3) =>
    if c.val = 0 then u.val else if c.val = 1 then v.val else u.val ^^^ v.val
  (∃ (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (readout : ℕ → Fin h → Fin t → D)
      (bias : ℕ → Fin h → Fin t → F),
    ∀ x i j, operand x i (a i j) * operand x i (b i j) =
      readout (run ask x) i j x + bias (run ask x) i j) ↔
  ∃ pick : Fin h → Fin t → Fin 3,
    let last := (List.finRange h).foldl (fun st i =>
      advance st (fun j => selectMask (a i j) (b i j) (pick i j))) ((0, {0}) : ℕ × Finset ℕ)
    last.1 + Nat.log2 last.2.card ≤ d

Keep the span of combinations vanishing on all forgotten sites. Close it under adding the chosen five-bit masks. Dropping the current coordinate costs one rank exactly when an odd mask is present. Shift the even masks to obtain the next boundary space. Charge its dimension at the end. All later masks vanish on every forgotten site. Allow 120 to 240 minutes.

changed.statement:
∀ (n m : Nat) (A : Fin n → Fin m → Bool), 3 ≤ n → 3 ≤ m →
  let rowLE := fun i k : Fin n => ∀ j, A i j = true → A k j = true
  let colLE := fun j l : Fin m => ∀ i, A i j = true → A i l = true
  let rc := fun i k : Fin n => rowLE i k ∨ rowLE k i
  let cc := fun j l : Fin m => colLE j l ∨ colLE l j
  Function.Injective A → Function.Injective (fun j i => A i j) →
  (∀ i, ∃ k, ¬ rc i k) → (∀ j, ∃ l, ¬ cc j l) →
  ∀ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C →
  C.size ≤ n + m - 1 →
  PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A (C.size + (n+m-5))

changed.title: Exact minimum support for averaging every cyclic translate of an integer score list of length a power of two
changed.statement:
∀ (a : ℕ) (v : Fin (2^a) → ℕ),
  let I := Fin (2^a)
  let side := fun (j h : ℕ) => (Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun i => i.val % (2^(j+1)) = h)
  let active := (Finset.range a).filter (fun j => (List.range (2^j)).any (fun h => decide (
    (∑ i ∈ side j h, v i) ≠ ∑ i ∈ side j (h+2^j), v i)))
  let q := 2^active.card
  let coins := (Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun s =>
    (List.range a).all (fun j => !(s.val.testBit j) || decide (j ∈ active)))
  let balanced := fun (p : I → ℝ) =>
    ∀ i i' : I, (∑ s : I, p s * (v (i+s) : ℝ)) = ∑ s : I, p s * (v (i'+s) : ℝ)
  coins.card = q ∧ balanced (fun s => if s ∈ coins then 1/(q : ℝ) else 0) ∧
    ∀ p : I → ℝ, (∀ s, 0 ≤ p s) → (∑ s, p s) = 1 →
      (balanced p ↔ ∀ j ∈ active, ∀ h ∈ Finset.range (2^j),
        (∑ s ∈ side j h, p s) = ∑ s ∈ side j (h+2^j), p s) ∧
      (balanced p → q ≤ ((Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun s => 0 < p s)).card)

A nonzero rational score remainder is invertible there over the rationals by cyclotomic irreducibility, hence also over the reals. The product is constant across indices exactly when all nontrivial factors divide it. At every active level each positive parent mass splits into two positive children. Choosing just the active bits uniformly gives both this support size and the sibling equalities.

changed.title: Budgeted selector circuits realize every dyadic coin pattern with a sharp support requirement within the specified circuit family
changed.statement:
∀ (a k : ℕ), 6 ≤ a → 2*2^a ≤ k → ∀ J : Finset (Fin a),
  let r := 2^a
  let N := 2^k
  let I := Fin r
  let X := Fin N
  let q := 2^J.card
  let L := N/(128*r)
  let marked := (Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun j => ∀ h ∈ J, j.val.testBit h.val = false)
  let coins := (Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun s =>
    ∀ h : Fin a, s.val.testBit h.val = true → h ∈ J)
  let label := fun j : I => 2^(r+j.val)
  let loss := fun (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (D : Finset I) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (X × X)).filter (fun z =>
      C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach z.1 z.2) ≠
        xor (z.1.val.testBit (z.2.val % r)) (decide (Nat.xor z.1.val z.2.val ∈ D.image label)))).card
  let E := L*marked.card
  ∃ rot : I → PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
    (∀ s, (∀ g ∈ (rot s).gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧
      16*((rot s).gates.countP (fun g => g.inputs.length == 2)) ≤ 33*N ∧
      ∀ D : Finset I, loss (rot s) D + 2*L*((D.image (fun j => j+s)) ∩ marked).card = N*D.card+E) ∧
    coins.card = q ∧ q*E = N/128 ∧
    (∀ D : Finset I, r*(∑ s ∈ coins, loss (rot s) D) + q*2*D.card*E = q*r*(N*D.card+E)) ∧
    ∀ t : ℕ, 0 < t → t < r → ∀ p : I → ℝ, (∀ s, 0 ≤ p s) → (∑ s, p s) = 1 →
      (∀ D : Finset I, D.card = t →
        (r : ℝ)*(∑ s : I, p s * (loss (rot s) D : ℝ)) + 2*(t : ℝ)*(E : ℝ) ≤
          (r : ℝ)*((N*t+E : ℕ) : ℝ)) →
      q ≤ ((Finset.univ : Finset I).filter (fun s => 0 < p s)).card

changed.title: For positive address and border parameters a tagged selector forces a squared deficit in the two-slot gate budget
changed.statement:
∀ (k a d : ℕ), (0 < a ∧ 2^a ≤ k ∧ 0 < d ∧ 2*d+1 ≤ k) →
  let N := 2^k
  let m := k-d
  let h := 2^m
  let δ := 2^(m-2)
  let low := fun (i j : Fin N) =>
    ((Finset.range m).filter (fun l => i.val.testBit l && j.val.testBit l)).card
  let cross := fun (i j : Fin N) => ((Finset.range d).filter (fun l =>
    i.val.testBit (m+l) && j.val.testBit 0 && j.val.testBit (l+1))).card
  let tag := fun (left right : Fin N) => (low left right + cross left right + cross right left)%2 == 1
  let r := 2^a
  let G := fun (x y : Fin N) => if x.val < h ∨ y.val < h then tag x y
    else x.val.testBit (y.val % r)
  PEqualNP.Represents.HasLitSize (k+k) (PEqualNP.Represents.adjFun (k := k) (l := k) G)
    (3*(r-1)+8*k+16*d+8) ∧
  ∀ (f g : Fin N → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
    (∀ gate ∈ C.gates, gate.inputs.length ≤ 2) →
    let e := (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin N × Fin N =>
      C.eval (PEqualNP.Represents.oneEach p.1 p.2) ≠
        xor (G p.1 p.2) (xor (f p.1) (g p.2)))).card
    let b := C.gates.countP (fun gate => gate.inputs.length == 2)
    ∀ v : ℕ, 0 < v → 17+2*(v-1) ≤ δ →
      (32*N-(15*b+54+44*(e/v)+2*h+2*a*(N/r)))^2 ≤ 4*e

With p labels left, at most e+p unordered pairs disagree in the bare switched selector. Expose every row outside this set. Its unordered decoder incurs exactly those disagreements. Apply the address histogram bound with cap N/r to get p²≤4e+(4+2aN/r)p. Square the positive part of p-4-2aN/r and substitute the extraction count.

changed.context: Normalize the live positive cone. An unread row would be inside every row, so each discarded line is live. Mark its input, then mark gates both of whose inputs are marked. The nonconstant kept output is unmarked. If d inputs and h gates are marked and b gates have exactly one marked operand, outgoing uses give d+h ≤ 2h+b. Set discarded inputs false. Every marked gate is zero. Each boundary OR aliases its other operand and each boundary AND is zero. Remove all h+b gates and reindex the kept inputs.
